title: I think I've been scammed
intro: Work through these steps in order. You do not have to do them alone — ask a friend, your hall tutor or your university to sit with you.

steps.title: Stop paying, right now
steps.detail: Do not send another transfer, top-up or deposit, even if you are told the money is refundable. Stopping early is the single most useful thing you can do.

steps.title: Call your bank's hotline
steps.detail: Use the number printed on the back of your card or in your banking app — never a number from the message. Ask them to freeze the transfer and note the case number.

links.label: Call the number on your card or app

steps.title: Report to the police
steps.detail: Call 999 if you are in danger right now. Otherwise call the 24-hour Anti-Scam Helpline on 18222 for advice, then file a report at any police station.

steps.title: Keep the evidence
steps.detail: Screenshot the listing, the chat, the payment confirmation and the account number you paid. Save them somewhere you can find later. Do not delete the conversation.

steps.title: Tell your university
steps.detail: Your student affairs or international office can help with accommodation, a temporary place to stay, and a letter if you need one. They have seen this before.

steps.title: Protect your identity
steps.detail: If you shared your HKID, bank details or a one-time code, change your banking passwords and ask your bank to watch the account. Do not share any new codes with anyone.

disclaimer: General information only, not legal advice. For a tenancy dispute, speak to the Rating and Valuation Department hotline or the Duty Lawyer Service.
